title: Shin splints
claims: Shin splints cause pain and tenderness along the front of the lower leg and usually happen after exercise such as running.

NHS self-care includes pain relief, icing for up to 20 minutes every 2 to 3 hours, switching temporarily to gentle exercise such as yoga or swimming, exercising on soft ground when ready, warming up and stretching.
NHS advises not continuing the exercise that caused the pain and not rushing back to the previous level.
NHS advises seeing a GP if pain worsens or does not improve, and contacting NHS 111 if pain is severe or the shin is injured.
NHS lists starting exercise after inactivity, running or jumping on hard surfaces, and poor running technique as risk factors.
